docs.title: vergil-fixture-rust-app
docs.text:
This is a Vergil test fixture. It has no users.

It holds a small Rust command-line application so that Vergil's support for Rust applications runs against a real one: local validation with vrg-validate, CI, the dependency and license audit, this docs site and the tagged release. Each fixture run adds one small increment to the program and drives it through Vergil's full cycle, from change to release.

Why the fixture exists, and how a fixture run works, is set out in the spec of epic vergil-project/.github#1091.

docs.title: What it exercises
docs.text:
• vrg-validate's Rust checks: cargo fmt, cargo clippy, cargo check, tests at 100% line coverage with cargo llvm-cov, and cargo deny against the fleet's packaged license policy.
  • Three real runtime dependencies, clap, anyhow and serde_json, for the audit and the dependency tooling to work on.
  • The fleet's CI and CD workflows, this site and the release.

Nothing it builds is published to a package registry.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: The fixture is a Cargo package with one binary, vergil-fixture-rust-app.

docs.title: Build and run
docs.text:
From a clone of the repository:

$ cargo run -- greet Ada
Hello, Ada

cargo build --release puts the binary at target/release/vergil-fixture-rust-app.

docs.title: Validate
docs.text:
As in every Vergil repo, validation runs in the Vergil dev container, and nothing else is the gate:

vrg-container-run -- vrg-validate

docs.title: Layout
docs.text: Path Holds src/main.rs the binary: parse the command line, run, set the exit code src/lib.rs run, which dispatches a parsed subcommand src/cli.rs the clap parser and the Command enum src/commands/ one module per subcommand, with its unit tests tests/cli.rs end-to-end tests that run the built binary

docs.title: Adding a subcommand
docs.text:
A fixture run grows the program by one subcommand at a time, with no restructuring:

  1. Add src/commands/<name>.rs with the subcommand's Args (when it takes any), its logic as a plain function, a run that writes the result, and unit tests.
  2. Declare the module in src/commands.rs.
  3. Add a variant to Command in src/cli.rs, and its arm to the match in run in src/lib.rs.
  4. Add its end-to-end tests to tests/cli.rs and its entry to the Usage page.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
vergil-fixture-rust-app <COMMAND>
Command Prints greet NAME a greeting for NAME sum [NUMBERS]... the sum of the integers max NUMBERS... the largest of the integers info the program's name and version as JSON

--help prints the commands, and --version prints the program's name and version.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 success 1 the command failed; the reason is on standard error, after error: 2 a usage error, such as a missing command or an argument that does not parse

docs.title: greet
docs.text:
Prints Hello, NAME.

$ vergil-fixture-rust-app greet Ada
Hello, Ada

A name that is empty or only whitespace is an error:

$ vergil-fixture-rust-app greet " "
error: the name must not be blank

docs.title: sum
docs.text:
Prints the sum of its arguments, which are 64-bit signed integers. Negative numbers need no --. With no arguments, the sum is 0.

$ vergil-fixture-rust-app sum 1 2 3
6
$ vergil-fixture-rust-app sum -4 2
-2

A sum outside the 64-bit signed range is an error:

$ vergil-fixture-rust-app sum 9223372036854775807 1
error: the sum overflows a 64-bit signed integer

docs.title: max
docs.text:
Prints the largest of its arguments, which are 64-bit signed integers. Negative numbers need no --.

$ vergil-fixture-rust-app max 1 3 2
3
$ vergil-fixture-rust-app max -4 -2
-2

With no arguments there is no largest number, so it is an error:

$ vergil-fixture-rust-app max
error: max needs at least one number

docs.title: info
docs.text:
Prints one line of compact JSON with the program's name and version:

$ vergil-fixture-rust-app info
{"name":"vergil-fixture-rust-app","version":"0.1.0"}

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• add the Rust CLI program and run CodeQL on it (#4)
  • feat(fixture): a small CLI with greet, sum and info subcommands

The fixture's program: a clap CLI with three subcommands, one module each, unit and end-to-end tests at 100% line coverage, the docs pages and the README. Runtime dependencies: clap, anyhow and serde_json. Epic vergil-project/.github#1091, plan Task 6d.

  • ci(security): run CodeQL on Rust so the required checks report

Remove run-codeql: false so the security job runs CodeQL on Rust. The CI-gates ruleset requires security / codeql and the GHAS CodeQL check, so every PR here was blocked with all checks green.

  • add the max subcommand (#8) max NUMBERS... prints the largest of its integers and fails when none are given. Its logic function carries a doctest, the first in the fixture, so the cargo test --doc step validates a real test. Ref vergil-project/vergil-fixture-rust-app#5
